h1: The 5 Best TV Stands with Storage of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best TV Stands with Storage: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: five TV stands with cabinets, drawers and shelves compared on TV size, storage layout and weight capacity for living rooms.
summary: The Giantex 55 to 70 inch stand is the best TV stand with storage: three open shelves, two soft-close cabinets and a drawer for $50 to $100. The Tribesigns is the answer for TVs up to 80 inches and the only one with stated load ratings. The JUSTOGO adds outlets and a mount, while the rustic Giantex trades capacity for looks.
intro: Storage on a TV stand only counts if it matches the gear you own. Three open shelves look tidy in a catalog and leave cables, game boxes and a router on permanent display. Small drawers do the opposite: they hide almost nothing, because a console, a soundbar and a streaming box do not fit inside a drawer built for remotes and chargers.

We ranked five stands from the spec sheets, scoring them on the Primea framework: stated TV size range, storage layout, weight capacities, hardware and price bucket. Each pick names exactly what it stores and how, so you can decide between closed cabinets and open shelves before you measure the wall. Weight ratings are listed only where the maker states one.

products.name: Giantex TV Stand for 55-70 Inch TV, Modern Entertainment Center with 3 Open Shelves, 2 Soft-Close Side Cabinets and Drawer
products.verdict: A balanced mix of open and closed storage.
products.description:
The Giantex 55 to 70 inch stand splits its storage the way a real living room needs it: three open center shelves for a console and streaming box that need airflow, and two soft-close side cabinets plus a drawer for everything you would rather not see. It is engineered wood with a two-tone finish.

It ranks first because the layout handles mixed gear and the $50 to $100 bracket undercuts every stand above third place. Soft-close hinges are a small feature with a daily payoff, since a slammed cabinet door rattles the TV and loosens hardware over years.

Buy it for a mid to large TV in a typical living room. The caveat is the missing weight rating: the listing does not state a capacity, so check the product page against your TV's weight before you buy.

products.name: Tribesigns 70.8 Inch Long TV Stand for 65/70/75 Inch TVs, Storage Cabinets & Shelves
products.verdict: The longest stand, with stated load ratings.
products.description:
The Tribesigns is 70.8 inches wide and fits 65 to 80 inch TVs, with concealed cabinets, an open center shelf and a reinforced center support leg. It is the only stand here that states load: 250 lbs overall and 35 lbs per shelf. That center leg matters on a stand this wide, because a long top panel sags under a heavy set without a mid support.

It ranks second because the Giantex covers most living rooms for less, while this one costs $100 to $200 and demands floor space. It earns its slot where nothing else works: an 80 inch screen on a wide wall.

Buy it for a very large TV and a wall that can take the length. Skip it if the wall is under 6 feet wide.
products.skipIf: The wall is under 6 feet wide.

products.name: JUSTOGO TV Stand with Mount and Power Outlet, TV Stand with Drawers Storage for 45-65 Inch TVs
products.verdict: Drawers, a mount and four outlets.
products.description:
The JUSTOGO is a one-box setup: two open shelves, three removable drawers, four power outlets and a built-in mount with three height levels and a 35 degree swivel each way. It lists TVs from 32 to 65 inches and ships with anti-tip hardware, in the $100 to $200 bracket.

It ranks third because mount hardware adds complexity and failure points that a plain console avoids, and the listing states no weight capacity. Against the Giantex 55 to 70 it is the only stand with built-in outlets, which clears a rat's nest of power strips behind the unit.

Buy it if you want everything in one cabinet and a TV near the middle of its range. Skip it if you prefer a plain console, or own a screen above 65 inches, where the 65 inch ceiling rules it out.
products.idealFor: People who want a one-box setup.

products.name: Giantex Rustic 65 Inch Entertainment Center with Pull-Out Drawer, Cabinet and 3 Shelves
products.verdict: A farmhouse look with a pull-out drawer.
products.description:
The rustic Giantex is built for a farmhouse room: distressed wood grain, barn-style hardware, one pull-out drawer, one cabinet and three open shelves, on engineered wood. It fits TVs up to 65 inches and costs $100 to $200.

The three open shelves are placed for remotes and a console that needs to talk to your TV, and the single cabinet gives you one closed space for clutter. It ranks fourth because it fits fewer screen sizes than the first two and lists no weight rating, and the modern Giantex above it costs less for more storage.

Buy it if the look is the point, since it works in a rustic or cottage-style room better than a two-tone modern stand. Skip it if your decor is modern or your TV runs past 65 inches, because style is the only thing it adds.

products.name: Giantex TV Stand for TV up to 55 Inch, 2 Drawers, Solid Wood Legs, White
products.verdict: A small white stand for 55 inch TVs.
products.description:
The compact Giantex is built for TVs up to 55 inches, with two fabric-front drawers, solid wood legs and a white finish, in the $50 to $100 bracket. The raised legs matter in practice: they let you vacuum underneath and keep a small stand from looking heavy in a bedroom.

It ranks last because it holds the least. Two drawers fit remotes, cables and a few discs, but no console, and the 55 inch limit shuts out any large screen. Next to the other Giantex stands, it trades storage for footprint.

Buy it for a bedroom or small apartment where a 55 inch TV is your ceiling. Skip it if you own a bigger screen or a game console, since there is no shelf for equipment and the drawers will not take it.
products.skipIf: You own a TV over 55 inches.

whatMatters.detail: A stand should be at least as wide as your TV, and the diagonal does not tell you that. The Tribesigns is 70.8 inches wide for 65 to 80 inch screens, while the compact Giantex suits TVs up to 55 inches. Measure the TV's actual width and feet spacing, then compare it to the stand's top surface in the listing.

Open shelves suit consoles and streaming boxes that need airflow and respond to a remote. Closed cabinets hide clutter. A mix, like the Giantex 55 to 70 inch with its three open shelves and two cabinets, handles both. Count how many open and closed compartments the listing names, and note the drawer sizes.

The top surface must carry your TV, and an unstated rating means you are guessing. Only the Tribesigns lists 250 lbs overall and 35 lbs per shelf. If a listing leaves out the capacity, as the Giantex stands do, check the full product page and compare it with your TV's weight before you buy.

Soft-close hinges stop cabinet doors from slamming, which saves the hardware and keeps vibration off your TV. Drawers keep small items tidy but hold less than cabinets. The Giantex 55 to 70 inch stand advertises soft-close cabinets in its title. Look for named hinges in the title or bullets rather than assuming.

Cables are the daily annoyance. Back panels with gaps make routing easier, and built-in outlets, as on the JUSTOGO, cut the visible clutter. Without cord access you end up with wires draped over the front of the unit. Look for cord ports, cutouts or an outlet strip in the listing, then check the images.

faq.q: How wide should a TV stand be?
faq.a: Wider than your TV, ideally with a few inches to spare on each side. Measure the TV's width, not the diagonal, then compare it to the stand's top width, such as the Tribesigns at 70.8 inches.

faq.q: Can I put a heavy TV on any of these?
faq.a: Check the weight rating on the product page first. Only the Tribesigns states an overall 250 lb capacity in the listing data, so for a heavy set it is the only one with a documented limit, and 35 lbs per shelf covers a soundbar and console.

faq.q: Is the JUSTOGO worth it over the Giantex 55-70?
faq.a: If you want outlets and a built-in mount, yes. For plain storage the Giantex 55 to 70 inch stand is simpler, has two soft-close cabinets, and costs less in the $50 to $100 bracket.

Plan about an hour and a helper, since the top panels are awkward to lift alone, on larger stands like the Tribesigns. Where anti-tip hardware is supplied, as on the JUSTOGO, anchor the stand to the wall before you set the TV on top.
Wipe engineered wood with a damp cloth, then dry it straight away with a soft towel. Avoid soaking the surface or the edges, where moisture swells the board, on the Giantex stands especially.

Yes, in homes with children or pets. A tall unit carrying a TV can tip when climbed on. The JUSTOGO ships with anti-tip hardware, so check what the other stands include and add your own anchor if needed.

finalTake: For most living rooms, the Giantex 55 to 70 inch stand is the right buy: open shelves for gear, soft-close cabinets for clutter and a drawer for small items. Pick the Tribesigns for an 80 inch screen and the only stated load rating. The JUSTOGO suits people who want outlets and a mount in one box. Measure the TV's width and check the weight rating before ordering.
